title: Unify bounded commit subjects and exact canonical Task-ID validation

supersedes_review.note: Independent review rejected this exact prior head against six findings (P1 x5, P2 x1). Every finding is addressed by the changes on top of that head described below; this evidence file describes the corrected state, not the rejected one.

owned: two deterministic bounded-commit-subject-prefix helpers (canonical_commit_subject_prefix, commit_subject_prefix_variants) shared by CI, the worker commit wrapper, and canonical done

exact-prefix cross-check between a commit subject's own prefix and its Task-ID trailer/expected task id in CI, worker_commit.py, and ai_status.py's done gate -- replacing a permissive substring-anywhere match that let a subject naming a different task (e.g. 'XYZ-001: mentions ABC-001') pass
duplicate/conflicting Task-ID (and other required) trailer rejection in CI, worker_commit.py, ai_status.py's done gate, and validate_merged_tooling_done
worker_commit.py preflight validation of subject identity and Task-ID trailer before staging/committing, with no ImportError fail-open fallback

removal of ai_status.py's second, looser trailer parser (parse_commit_metadata_lines) in favor of the shared check_commit_trailers.parse_trailers, imported lazily so scripts/git/ is only required by the code path that actually needs it

validate_merged_tooling_done now treats a present Task-ID trailer as canonical identity (exact match, no duplicates) instead of a whole-message substring/regex search that could not distinguish a mentioned id from a bound one
not_changing: approved_closeout_commit_ref / approved_closeout_metadata_ref merge-first-parent unwrapping and ancestry verification
scripts/git/check_commit_scope.py (a separate pre-commit hook script, not in this task's artifacts)
auto_integrator.py, worker_runner.py, supervisor.py, branch protection, credentials, or canonical JSON shape

validate_merged_tooling_done's Human/Ops + development_tooling authority and its reviewer-free direct-tooling exception -- only its identity check for a present Task-ID trailer changed; the legacy no-trailer whole-message regex fallback is preserved unchanged for commits that never carried one

short task-id behavior for an exempt subject (merge commit, OPS-DOC/OPS-REBASE housekeeping, promote/hotfix/publish): the literal id embedded anywhere in the subject (e.g. inside a merge commit's task/<id> branch name) still passes exactly as before
composes_with: the existing per-task PR review/merge flow used to recover PR #5639's own original approval

failure_reproduction.case: On dev 46bbfe935df1e68740569fb5dc6233897de98b0b, check_commit_trailers.check_message required subjects <=72 chars while ai_status.py's done-finalize gate required the literal, untruncated task id to appear in the subject. A 92-char generated task id (INTEGRATION-UNBLOCK-GOV-APPROVAL-AUTHORITY-PREREQUISITE-001-MERGE-STATE-BLOCKED-B14932FE23E9) cannot satisfy both: its genuine, independently-approved, merged (PR #5639, head 50adbe0c68cfcc5d42024061c91f86dedb45159c into c607359338026f4e440f62d052e19648d78d3f04) commit passed CI's bounded-subject check but could never satisfy done's literal-substring check.

codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.finding: P1: ai_status.py's module-level `from check_commit_trailers import parse_trailers` made every ai_status.py invocation require scripts/git/ to be importable, breaking .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py::RealProcessReviewHandoffRecoveryFlowTests::test_real_runner_queue_consumer_launches_exactly_one_owner_across_restart, whose _copy_tooling fixture only copies scripts/*.py (not scripts/git/).
codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.fix: the check_commit_trailers import (parse_trailers and duplicate_trailer_problems) is now lazy, loaded inside collect_done_delivery_metadata and validate_merged_tooling_done only -- the only two functions that need it.

codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.finding: P1: for task_id='A'*61 / description='fix', bound_commit_subject returns the valid, uncompacted 66-char subject, but canonical_commit_subject_prefix alone always compacted once the id crossed the ~60-char boundary regardless of description length, so check_message rejected the genuine formatter output.
codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.fix: common.commit_subject_prefix_variants(task_id) returns both the full uncompacted prefix and the compacted prefix; every consumer (check_commit_trailers.py, worker_commit.py, ai_status.py) now accepts either, since bound_commit_subject can legitimately emit either depending on the actual description length.

codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.finding: P1: worker_commit.py and ai_status.py used substring ('in subject') membership for the task-id/prefix check while CI used an exact prefix, so 'XYZ-001: mentions ABC-001' with Task-ID: ABC-001 was rejected by CI but accepted by worker preflight and owner metadata collection.
codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.fix: worker_commit.py and ai_status.py's done gate now compare the subject's own prefix (the text before its first ':') against the literal task id or commit_subject_prefix_variants, exactly as CI does, for any subject not covered by the trailer-presence exemption.
codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.regression_test: scripts/git/test_worker_commit.py::test_worker_commit_rejects_subject_naming_a_different_task (pre-existing on the rejected head, still passes), scripts/test_ai_status.py::DeliveryMetadataValidationTests::test_collect_done_delivery_metadata_rejects_bounded_prefix_for_wrong_task (pre-existing, still passes) -- both now driven by the exact-prefix check instead of a substring check that happened to agree on those specific fixtures

codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.finding: P1: none of the three consumers consistently rejected ambiguity: an identical duplicate Task-ID line passed everywhere (acceptable), but a conflicting duplicate (Task-ID: XYZ-001 then Task-ID: ABC-001) passed ai_status.py's owner metadata collection because parse_trailers keeps only the last value; the OPS-DOC-* style exemption accepted a Task-ID trailer naming a different task entirely; validate_merged_tooling_done accepted a wrong Task-ID trailer via a whole-message regex that only checked whether the *task's own* id appeared anywhere in the message, not whether the trailer agreed.
codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.fix: collect_done_delivery_metadata now runs check_commit_trailers.duplicate_trailer_problems over the required trailers before accepting metadata (rejecting conflicting duplicates), and separately -- even under the trailer-skip exemption -- rejects a present Task-ID trailer that does not match the task id. validate_merged_tooling_done now checks a present Task-ID trailer for exact match (and duplicate/conflict), falling back to the legacy whole-message regex only when no Task-ID trailer exists at all.

codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.finding: P1: worker_commit.py caught ImportError around the new common.canonical_commit_subject_prefix import and silently disabled the identity check (set the validator to None) rather than failing, so a worker whose PANTHEON_COMMAND_ROOT resolved to a command runtime missing the helper got no validation at all.
codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.fix: the try/except ImportError fail-open fallback is removed; common.canonical_commit_subject_prefix and commit_subject_prefix_variants are now hard, unconditional imports (matching the existing hard-required common.write_activity_log import in the same file) that raise a clear ModuleNotFoundError instead of silently downgrading validation.
codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.regression_test: scripts/git/test_worker_commit.py (full suite, unmodified except new cases) -- no test exercises or expects the removed fallback; grepped the repository for any consumer of the removed sentinel (canonical_commit_subject_prefix is None) and found none

codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.finding: P2: the evidence manifest committed alongside the rejected head recorded scripts/git/worker_commit.py's SHA256 as 740c54c8... but the actual committed file was 773761b7....
codex2_review_findings_and_fixes.fix: this evidence file's checksums section is regenerated from the exact files in this commit (see below); worker_commit.py's content has changed again as part of the fixes above, so its checksum here reflects the corrected file, not either prior stale value.

failure_reproduction.positive_case_unaffected: The immutable, already-merged PR #5639 commit (50adbe0c68cfcc5d42024061c91f86dedb45159c, real 92-char Task-ID, subject 'INTEGRATION-UNBLOCK-GOV-APPROVAL-AU: record accepted source merge') was read directly via `git show` and passed CI, worker preflight, and owner metadata collection unchanged before and after every fix above -- verified with a standalone reproduction script mirroring the reviewer's isolated-fixture method (git/context mocked; worker stopped before staging; no live done/approval/merge claimed).

implementation.shared_helpers: common.canonical_commit_subject_prefix(task_id, max_len=72) is the deterministic compacted-if-necessary prefix; common.commit_subject_prefix_variants(task_id, max_len=72) returns (full_prefix, canonical_commit_subject_prefix(...)) -- the pair a validator without the description must accept. bound_commit_subject derives its own prefix/compaction from the same two extracted lower-level helpers (_normalized_task_prefix, _compacted_task_prefix), so it can only ever emit one of the two values commit_subject_prefix_variants returns.
implementation.ci_check_commit_trailers: check_message cross-checks the subject's own prefix against commit_subject_prefix_variants(<Task-ID trailer>) (accepting either) when prefix_required is true and a Task-ID trailer is present, and rejects any required trailer that appears more than once with conflicting values (duplicate_trailer_problems, pre-existing on the rejected head, unmodified).
implementation.worker_commit_preflight: worker_commit.py's preflight compares the subject's own prefix (text before its first ':') exactly against --task-id or commit_subject_prefix_variants(--task-id) -- not a substring check -- and separately requires exactly one Task-ID trailer in the body equal to --task-id. The common.py identity-helper import is now a hard dependency (ModuleNotFoundError on failure), matching the existing hard write_activity_log import.
implementation.ai_status_done_gate: collect_done_delivery_metadata computes commit_subject_skips_trailer_check once and reuses it: for an exempt subject the task id may appear anywhere (unchanged); for every other subject, its own prefix must exactly equal the literal task id or one of commit_subject_prefix_variants(task_id). check_commit_trailers.parse_trailers and duplicate_trailer_problems are imported lazily (inside the function) via a new _commit_trailer_checker() loader, replacing the removed module-level import and the removed duplicate parser parse_commit_metadata_lines. Conflicting required-trailer values are rejected before field comparison; a present Task-ID trailer under the exemption path must still match the task id.
implementation.validate_merged_tooling_done_narrowed: still resolves the exact delivery commit via the existing _validated_reconcile_delivery/_merged_commit ancestry-verified path with no first-parent unwrapping and no product-review-proof requirement (Human/Ops + development_tooling authority unchanged). It now inspects the commit body for a Task-ID trailer via the same lazily-loaded checker: if one is present it must exactly match the task id (rejecting duplicates/conflicts and mismatches); only when no Task-ID trailer exists at all does it fall back to the original word-boundary-guarded whole-message regex.

review_decision.note: Independently verify: commit_subject_prefix_variants replaces the single-value canonical_commit_subject_prefix comparison everywhere an exact-prefix check is made (CI, worker_commit.py, ai_status.py done gate), and specifically the 61-char/short-description boundary case; the exact-prefix (not substring) rule in worker_commit.py and ai_status.py now agrees with CI on 'XYZ-001: mentions ABC-001'; conflicting/duplicated Task-ID trailers are now rejected consistently across CI, worker_commit.py, ai_status.py's done gate, and validate_merged_tooling_done; the OPS-DOC/OPS-REBASE/merge trailer-presence exemption no longer accepts a present-but-wrong Task-ID trailer; worker_commit.py's identity-helper import is a hard dependency with no ImportError fail-open; ai_status.py's check_commit_trailers import is lazy and .orchestrator/test_supervisor.py::RealProcessReviewHandoffRecoveryFlowTests::test_real_runner_queue_consumer_launches_exactly_one_owner_across_restart passes again; and the full combined test run.
